hyperedges.label: What actually makes the instrument unbiased
The measurement chain: flow, dT, aux power, the reading
The safety chain, hardware to supervisor

nodes.label: Read the flat 'key: value' pairs. Uses PyYAML when present.
nodes.norm_label: read the flat 'key: value' pairs. uses pyyaml when present.

nodes.label: Back-calculation anti-windup
nodes.rationale: Chosen over conditional integration because its correction term is exactly zero when the output is not clipped: no branch to get wrong, no discontinuity at the limit. T_t = Kp/Ki = tau_e.

nodes.label: Boundary B1 - the inner chamber
nodes.rationale: Every watt dissipated inside B1 that is not metered is reported as DUT loss one-for-one, because the model's D_u = -1 entry can only cancel what it was told about. The corollary is counter-intuitive: the guard heater, the largest power in the rig, needs the LEAST accurate measurement of anything, because the closed guard loop drives its DC gain to the reading to zero.

nodes.label: Disturbance observer, energy-balance form
nodes.rationale: P_hat = P_meas + (C_i+C_w) d(theta_bar)/dt falls straight out of the energy balance with the guard nulled. No observer gain to tune and no per-flow gain table, and it inherits the closed loop's exact unbiasedness because the derivative is zero at steady state.

nodes.label: The dT tare is per flow range
nodes.norm_label: the dt tare is per flow range
nodes.rationale: It absorbs probe mismatch AND pump work AND tube heat exchange, and the last two are flow dependent. ~0.5 W of pump work at 300 mL/min is 26 mK - the same order as the thing being measured. Never carry one tare across ranges.

nodes.label: The guard null loop
nodes.rationale: Servos the gap to the chamber so the leak term dies. Without it the rig is a ~1.3 % instrument, an order of magnitude outside the +-1 W target.

nodes.label: Heaters driven in WATTS, not duty
nodes.norm_label: heaters driven in watts, not duty
nodes.rationale: The model's gains are W/K. Sending a PI output in watts straight to a duty cycle multiplies the loop gain by V^2/R - a number nobody wrote down that drifts with rail sag and heater temperature. An inner power loop closed on the INA226 makes the model's gains transfer unchanged.

nodes.label: The integrator IS the accuracy
nodes.rationale: Proportional guard alone recovers 83 % of the deficit; the last 0.34 W is bought by one state. 'Add integral action' and 'make the calorimeter unbiased' are the same sentence - which is why anti-windup is not optional.

nodes.label: The null gate |e| < P_acc / G_gap
nodes.rationale: 1.79 K. Transient breaches at and above 150 W are NORMAL - |e| peaks at 1.91 K because the reference moves 20x faster than the loop that must follow it. Only a breach that survives past the settling budget is a fault; get that wrong and the first run faults out on physics.

nodes.label: The 1 Hz control tick
nodes.rationale: Right twice over: faster sampling crowds every discrete pole onto z=1, AND starves the integrator's float ULP - at 1 ms the per-tick increment is below float32 epsilon and the integrator silently freezes.

nodes.label: Shadow mode
nodes.rationale: The observer is computed and logged every tick but never gates a point until an NVS flag is flipped. One boolean, and it is the difference between a validated speed-up and an unvalidated one.

nodes.label: The steady gate |dP/dt| < P_thr / tau_dom
nodes.rationale: Gated on the READING, never on a temperature: the chamber air is dominated by 15 s modes and settles long before the reading does. The threshold is per point - a hard-coded W/h number is ~3x wrong at one end of the range.

nodes.label: tau_dom = max((C_i+C_w)/mcp, tau_e)
nodes.rationale: Computed rather than tabulated. Checked against the model's own two corners: 816.7 s vs 807.6 s (+1.1 %) and 297.0 s vs 293.6 s (+1.2 %), both conservative.

nodes.label: Carrier board overlay (ESP32-S3-DevKitC-1-N8R8)
nodes.rationale: Transcribed from Board/Design.md's J1/J3 pin tables. Every pin, address and bus in the shipping rig lives here and nowhere else, which is what made the port one file.

nodes.label: Dev-kit overlay (Waveshare ESP32-S3-LCD-1.47B)
nodes.rationale: Same device set and same aliases as the carrier board, so the bench build is a rehearsal rather than a different program. Disables the microSD slot and RGB LED to free pins and SPI2.

nodes.label: GPIO8 claimed for the INA226 wired-OR ALERT
nodes.norm_label: gpio8 claimed for the ina226 wired-or alert
nodes.rationale: PROPOSED, not transcribed. Design.md leaves GPIO8 as the one spare for 'an NTC or an interlock sense line', but it already replaced the NTC with an I2C sensor at 0x48 to avoid spending this pin. Spending it here makes over-current on two 8.3 A rails a hardware-timed trip. Delete the property and the firmware falls back to the software check.

nodes.label: Devicetree as data (D10)
nodes.rationale: No .c file names a pin, an address or a bus. That is what made porting from the bench dev kit to the carrier board an added overlay rather than a rewrite.

nodes.label: Fan health needs two signals
nodes.rationale: A tach proves something in the chain turns; only the rail current, against a signature learned at POST, can see ONE stopped fan in a PST daisy chain. They fail differently, which is the point.

nodes.label: The carrier board has no display
nodes.norm_label: the carrier board has no display
nodes.rationale: Its pin budget spends all 23 usable GPIOs. The LVGL panel exists only on the dev-kit build; on the carrier board the interface is the web dashboard, the UART console, and the BOOT button bound to STOP. A decision to make, not an oversight.

nodes.label: The N8R8 needs the espressif-psram-8M snippet
nodes.norm_label: the n8r8 needs the espressif-psram-8m snippet
nodes.rationale: The upstream esp32s3_devkitc board file includes esp32s3_wroom_n8.dtsi - the N8, no PSRAM. The snippet is what makes the build match the module actually fitted.

nodes.label: Two board targets, no app.overlay
nodes.rationale: Zephyr prefers boards/<target>.overlay when one exists and falls back to app.overlay only if none is found, so keeping both would mean an overlay that silently applies to some builds.

nodes.label: Web dashboard (single file, gzipped into flash)
nodes.norm_label: web dashboard (single file, gzipped into flash)
nodes.rationale: No CDN and no web font: the rig is LAN-only by design, so an external font request would fail anyway and the fallback stack IS the design. ~5.5 kB compressed.

nodes.label: wifi.conf - radio + WebSocket fragment
nodes.rationale: Split out because CONFIG_WIFI_ESP32 hard-selects MBEDTLS, which needs the tf-psa-crypto module. The base build therefore works on a workspace that has never fetched it.

nodes.label: params.yaml is the single source of truth
nodes.norm_label: params.yaml is the single source of truth
nodes.rationale: The classic failure of model-based control is not a wrong model, it is the PORT. Deriving the firmware's constants from the same file the simulation reads removes that failure class; the params hash is logged with every point so a stale header is detectable rather than silent.

nodes.label: The control core has no Zephyr dependency
nodes.norm_label: the control core has no zephyr dependency
nodes.rationale: The same object code links into the firmware, a host test build, and the Python simulation via ctypes - so tuning happens against the code that will actually run.

nodes.label: Stream state, not pixels
nodes.rationale: One JSON snapshot per second; the panel and any browser each render their own layout. A screen-scrape mirror would be locked to 172 px and could only be upscaled.

nodes.label: The I2C mux needs explicit init priorities
nodes.norm_label: the i2c mux needs explicit init priorities
nodes.rationale: i2c_tca954x.c has a BUILD_ASSERT that channels initialise after the root, and both default to CONFIG_I2C_INIT_PRIORITY - so the driver fails to BUILD the moment a mux appears in the tree.

nodes.label: One door for every command
nodes.rationale: The panel, the shell and the WebSocket all call sys_cmd_submit(). 'Local has priority' is therefore true by construction: there is no second path to an actuator.

nodes.label: Three threads, not four
nodes.rationale: The architecture note's fourth thread existed to run a 10 Hz A/B chop across a MULTIPLEXED RTD front end. With one converter per probe there is nothing to chop, and a 1 s sensor skew costs 0.34 mW - so a separate thread would buy races, not watts.

nodes.label: The inner fan duty is frozen for the campaign
nodes.norm_label: the inner fan duty is frozen for the campaign
nodes.rationale: Changing it changes P_aux and UA_rad at the same time - two model parameters at once, which invalidates every point before and after. Enforced in code, not left to discipline.

nodes.label: calorimeter,thermal-zone binding
nodes.rationale: Zone membership in devicetree is what turns 'make the guard zonal' from a refactor into adding a phandle.

nodes.label: Bring-up ladder F0-F8
nodes.rationale: F3 is the gate: if a known 100 W does not read back as 100 W, nothing above F3 means anything. F8 must be done by actually breaking things, not by reading code.

nodes.label: The isothermal soak
nodes.rationale: Before anything is powered the rig genuinely IS isothermal - a free, very strong reference. One procedure, three payoffs: relative calibration, a wiring self-test, and the POST's plausibility gate. Averaging cannot substitute: parts from one reel have correlated offsets.

nodes.label: The substitution check
nodes.rationale: Inject a known 100 W and confirm the meter reads it. The whole instrument in miniature.

nodes.label: Zones, not sensors
nodes.rationale: A zone is a node plus the sensors that measure it, averaged with dead ones excluded. Making the guard zonal is adding phandles to the overlay.

nodes.label: The heater interlock
nodes.rationale: Flow above minimum AND every zone sensor valid and fresher than 3 ticks AND every node below its limit AND no latched fault. The middle clause is the one people leave out and the one that burns rigs.

nodes.label: The safety thread never touches a bus
nodes.norm_label: the safety thread never touches a bus
nodes.rationale: A hung I2C bus cannot hang the safety thread - which matters because a hung bus is also exactly what freezes the value the guard integrator is accumulating against.

nodes.label: Software over-current backstop
nodes.rationale: The only over-current cover the three INA3221 rails have - that part has no ALERT pin here - and what survives if the schematic spends GPIO8 elsewhere.

nodes.label: A reading is a triple, not a float
nodes.norm_label: a reading is a triple, not a float
nodes.rationale: Value, timestamp, flags. A hung I2C bus does not report an error - it reports the LAST VALUE FOREVER, and the guard PI will integrate against a plausible constant while the chamber climbs. Staleness detection is the difference between a fault and a fire.

nodes.label: Three safety tiers
nodes.rationale: Tier 0 is hardware with no firmware in it at all; tier 1 is the bus-free safety thread at 10 Hz; tier 2 is the supervisor, whose faults abort the POINT rather than the power.

nodes.label: The turbine is the meter; the pump is the actuator
nodes.norm_label: the turbine is the meter; the pump is the actuator
nodes.rationale: An earlier plan made the stepper's step count primary. That was reversed: there is no step-count metrology anywhere. The command-vs-measurement disagreement is what makes a slipped tube or air lock loud instead of a plausible wrong answer.

nodes.label: The calorimeter equation P = rho*V*cp*dT - P_aux
nodes.norm_label: the calorimeter equation p = rho*v*cp*dt - p_aux
nodes.rationale: Density is evaluated at the meter's own temperature and c_p at the mean of the two ends. A fixed density would cost ~0.90 W of bias at 150 W - about one watt for two polynomials.

nodes.label: SPI sets the stepper's run current
nodes.norm_label: spi sets the stepper's run current
nodes.rationale: Zephyr has no in-tree TMC5160 driver and its stepper API would take STEP generation away from LEDC - which this rig needs in hardware, because the pulse rate IS the flow command. So SPI does one job: the current limit a cheaper driver would have soldered into a sense resistor.
